title: Daily Market Digest: August 19, 2026
subtitle: Wall Street Extends Declines Amid Tech Selloff and Anticipation of Fed Minutes

items.headline: U.S. Stocks Continue Bearish Trend; Tech and AI Sectors Face Headwinds
items.summary: U.S. equity markets are extending a three-session bearish trend on Wednesday, August 19, 2026, as investors react to ongoing selloffs in technology and artificial intelligence stocks. Rising treasury yields and elevated oil prices are also contributing to a cautious sentiment across the board. The market remains sensitive to geopolitical tensions and awaits the release of the Federal Reserve's latest meeting minutes later today, which could offer insights into future monetary policy. Not financial advice.

items.headline: 4D Molecular Therapeutics Leads Gainers
items.summary: 4D Molecular Therapeutics saw a significant surge, gaining 19.3% in today's trading.

items.headline: AXT Experiences Strong Growth
items.summary: Semiconductor materials company AXT climbed 17.6% today.

items.headline: EyePoint Pharmaceuticals Plummets
items.summary: EyePoint Pharmaceuticals experienced a sharp decline, dropping 67.0% during the session.

items.headline: Carvana Shares Fall
items.summary: Online used car retailer Carvana saw its shares decline by 7.3%.

items.headline: FOMC Minutes Release Eyed by Investors
items.summary: Investors are keenly awaiting the release of the U.S. Federal Reserve's July meeting minutes today, August 19, 2026. The minutes are expected to provide further clarity on the central bank's stance regarding interest rates, following the FOMC's decision to keep rates unchanged at 3.50-3.75% in July, despite three dissents for a rate hike.

items.headline: Major Retailers Report Earnings Today
items.summary: Several prominent retailers are scheduled to report earnings before the market open today, August 19, 2026, including Target, TJX Companies, and Lowe's. These reports will offer insights into consumer spending and the broader retail sector's health.

items.headline: Tech and AI Stocks Continue to Lead Market Downturn
items.summary: The technology and semiconductor sectors remained significant laggards in the previous session (August 18), with continued declines in AI-related stocks. This trend is driven by concerns that AI valuations may have become stretched and doubts about the long-term profitability of AI investments.

items.headline: Rising Treasury Yields and Oil Prices Add to Market Pressure
items.summary: Global borrowing costs reached fresh highs on Tuesday, with the interest rate on U.S. 30-year borrowing hitting 5.33%, its highest since June 2007. This, coupled with elevated oil prices amidst uncertainty in the Middle East, is dampening market sentiment.
